justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are fulfilled: Video Media Server handles video consultations (R-01), Pharmacy Integration Gateway orchestrates cross-border e-prescriptions (R-02), AI Symptom Checker Container assesses triage urgency (R-03), and Patient Consent Service manages granular consent per purpose (R-04).
justifications.performance_efficiency: Redis caching tiers in Data Storage and Patient Consent Service eliminate round-trips for consent checks. Video Media Server uses LiveKit SFU simulcast and ABR Controller for dynamic bandwidth scaling, supported by GCP Pub/Sub asynchronous event publishing.
justifications.compatibility: Pharmacy Integration Gateway uses an Adapter Engine (Go/Apache Camel) connecting via mTLS to EU National E-Prescription Gateways and HL7 FHIR REST APIs for US Pharmacy Networks. Data Storage also leverages PostgreSQL with native FHIR extensions.
justifications.usability: Patients, Licensed Clinicians, and Compliance Officers interact via a unified Flutter/Web 'Client Apps' container. Degraded mode mechanisms enhance usability in rural low-bandwidth settings, though role-specific interface operational nuances are left to client state management.
justifications.reliability: R-06 is handled via LiveKit SDK Video Adaptation, ABR Controller simulcast switching, and TURN Infrastructure fallback for <300 kbit/s links. Offline Sync & Local Storage (SQLCipher) and API Gateway Circuit Breakers safeguard continuous operations.
justifications.security: Rigorous security includes Envoy Auth/Policy Enforcement Filter, mTLS with SPIFFE/SPIRE, and regional database isolation (PostgreSQL EU/US). Audit & Traceability Logger and Ledger Storage Adapter write immutable logs to WORM GCP Cloud Storage for MDR and HIPAA/GDPR.
justifications.maintainability: The design exhibits high modularity with decoupled containers and clean internal components (e.g., Triage Engine, Prescription Orchestrator, Adapter Engine). Well-defined gRPC and REST interfaces with mTLS isolate domain logic, simplifying testing and component replacement.
justifications.portability: Explicitly targets GCP regions europe-west3 and us-central1 with isolated Cloud SQL and Cloud Storage. Uses portable containerized stacks (Go, Node.js, Python FastAPI, LiveKit SFU, Envoy) easily deployed across target regions.

PERF-01.justification: LiveKit SFU handles high-concurrency WebRTC sessions and Redis caches states to meet connection targets. However, dynamic auto-scaling of SFU instances and TURN nodes under sudden flu season surges is not explicitly detailed.
sensitivity_points: WebRTC SFU routing capacity and TURN relay bandwidth during concurrent connection spikes.
tradeoffs: Resource overhead of overprovisioned SFU instances versus connection setup latency under peak load.

PERF-02.justification: A volume of 50,000 requests per hour (~14 req/s) is easily handled by FastAPI and PyTorch triage services. Asynchronous logging to Cloud Storage ensures inference responses return well under the 3-second threshold.
sensitivity_points: Model inference latency and asynchronous dispatch of audit logs during peak throughput.
tradeoffs: Model complexity and accuracy versus inference latency and compute consumption.

AVAIL-01.justification: The architecture explicitly features an ABR Controller, LiveKit SDK dynamic bitrate adaptation with audio-fallback mode, and offline encrypted SQLite storage, preventing call drops and securing clinical notes at 200 kbit/s.
sensitivity_points: Threshold sensitivity of bitrate adaptation and seamless audio fallback activation under bandwidth drops.
tradeoffs: Visual fidelity degradation versus maintaining continuous consultation audio and clinical note capture.

AVAIL-02.justification: The architecture defines only a single US region (us-central1) and strictly isolates data. If us-central1 fails entirely, no secondary US region exists to restore services within one hour while maintaining US data residency.
sensitivity_points: Provisioning of multi-region US infrastructure to handle catastrophic single-region cloud outages.
tradeoffs: Infrastructure cost of redundant in-country regions versus meeting disaster recovery RTO objectives.

MOD-01.justification: The Pharmacy Integration Gateway cleanly isolates national protocol differences within the Adapter Engine using Apache Camel, keeping the Prescription Orchestrator unchanged when adding a new EU standard.
sensitivity_points: Modularity and decoupling of Apache Camel integration routes for heterogeneous national e-prescription interfaces.
tradeoffs: Abstraction overhead of Camel integration framework versus isolation of protocol modifications.

MOD-02.justification: Model outputs, inputs, and versions are captured by the Audit & Traceability Logger and stored in WORM storage. However, blue/green rollout or version rollback mechanisms for the containerized model are not detailed.
sensitivity_points: Accurate metadata tagging of model versions on every inference output for traceability.
tradeoffs: Storage overhead of immutable input/output version logging versus compliance and diagnostic traceability.

SEC-01.justification: Cross-region access is prevented by isolated regional databases and enforced by the Gateway Auth/Policy Enforcement Filter and Core Telehealth Consent Verifier, requiring explicit consent lookup before retrieving US records.
sensitivity_points: Synchronous enforcement of patient consent verification before cross-region query dispatch.
tradeoffs: Cross-region query latency overhead versus strict enforcement of HIPAA/GDPR data residency boundaries.

SEC-02.justification: Consent withdrawal triggers real-time cache invalidation via GCP Pub/Sub and updates Redis, stopping data access immediately (well within 24 hours), while the WORM storage adapter provides verifiable audit logs.
sensitivity_points: Real-time broadcast and invalidation of cached consent across distributed services via Pub/Sub.
tradeoffs: Distributed cache invalidation messaging complexity versus guaranteed rapid enforcement of consent revocations.
